correctness.rationale: For odd bicliques each local majority is strict and determines the update opinion of the opposite part. If both local majorities match, they cannot change, and every vertex rings within finite time. If opposed, exactly i initially positive first-part and b-j initially negative second-part first-clock rings matter until one of two exact thresholds \(r=i-u\) or \(s=v+1-j\) is reached. Their iid exponential first-clock ranks give a uniform subset of size r+s-1, hence the stated hypergeometric tail; color swap handles the reverse case. Hitting times are sums of independent \(E/h\), with mean log(\(x/(1-y)\))+O(1/N) and critical variance (2x-1)/(x λ(1-λ)N), and Lyapunov gives the stated normal CDF. Exact verifier replay checked 1,764 independent absorbing recurrences, 144 full first-clock permutations and 820 symmetry cases; finite tests are not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: A complete natural tie-free graph family has an exact answer for every binary initial configuration, rather than a selected example or one-step estimate. The large-size outcome depends on \(x+y\) independent of part-size weights; the critical width and exact Gaussian constant give a genuine predictive asymptotic invariant. The initial global minority can win nearly surely despite occupying only \(61/200\) of all vertices. The theorem thus exposes a structural limitation of global population-headcount heuristics and supplies a reproducible social-learning benchmark.
